briefs.headline: Reds beat the Braves 7-6 on Hector Rodriguez's two-run homer
briefs.summary: Atlanta scored four in the first off Brady Singer on Thursday, but Carlos Jorge's first career homer, Elly De La Cruz's 30th and Rodriguez's sixth, in the sixth, took the finale. Emilio Pagan earned his 25th save.

briefs.headline: Pirates beat the Cardinals 2-1 behind Paul Skenes
briefs.summary: Skenes allowed three hits and one run over 6 1/3 innings with eight strikeouts Thursday at PNC Park. Spencer Horwitz's eighth-inning sacrifice fly scored Ronny Simon, and Mason Montgomery struck out the side for his 17th save.

briefs.headline: Rodriguez says Oklahoma State's Mestemaker gets rid of the ball in 1.8 seconds
briefs.summary: The Cowboys have allowed three sacks in three games and average a play every 23.47 seconds, MetroNews reported Thursday. WVU, undefeated in three games, has run on 163 of 206 plays ahead of Saturday's 7 p.m. ET kickoff in Morgantown.

briefs.headline: Marshall uses quarterback Khalil Wilkins at three positions
briefs.summary: The former WVU player has lined up at quarterback, slot and receiver and on special teams, with 109 all-purpose yards in three games, the Herald-Dispatch reported Friday. Marshall closes nonconference play against Gardner-Webb on Saturday.

briefs.headline: Allen, Hill and Iosivas miss a second Bengals practice
briefs.summary: Jonathan Allen (rest/knee), B.J. Hill (Achilles) and Andrei Iosivas (thumb) did not practice Wednesday or Thursday, the team's injury report said. Steelers back Rico Dowdle (toe) also sat out both days before Sunday's 1 p.m. ET game.

briefs.headline: Orlando Brown Jr. ties his father's 129 games in Pittsburgh on Sunday
briefs.summary: The Bengals left tackle said Thursday his 129th NFL game matches the late Orlando 'Zeus' Brown Sr., who played for the Browns and Ravens. Teammates elected Dexter Lawrence II their NFLPA representative this week, the team said.

briefs.headline: Browns plan to contain Bryce Young, who has 648 passing yards
briefs.summary: Carolina leads the NFL with 312.5 passing yards per game and Young is tied for the lead with six touchdown passes, the team wrote Thursday. Quincy Williams called him 'a point guard' ahead of Sunday's 1 p.m. ET game in Cleveland.

briefs.headline: Liverpool close to naming Julian Ward sporting director
briefs.summary: Ward, who previously held the job for one season and has been Fenway Sports Group's technical director, would replace Richard Hughes, who left for Al Hilal this month, ESPN reported Wednesday, citing sources. The league resumes Oct. 10.

briefs.headline: Kirishima throws Onosato and cuts the yokozuna's Aki basho lead to one
briefs.summary: Ozeki (champion) Kirishima won Friday's Day 13 bout in Tokyo by shitatenage (underarm throw), leaving the yokozuna (grand champion) at 11 wins and two losses. Aonishiki and Asanoyama trail by one in the yusho (championship) race.

briefs.headline: Asanoyama forces out Atamifuji to stay a win behind Onosato
briefs.summary: The No. 6 maegashira (rank-and-file wrestler) beat the sekiwake (third-highest rank) by yorikiri (frontal force out) Friday for his 10th win. Ozeki Aonishiki's katasukashi (under-shoulder swing down) of Kotozakura kept him level.

briefs.headline: Onosato meets Kotozakura on Day 14 and needs both chasers to lose to clinch
briefs.summary: The JSA card sends Aonishiki against Kirishima and Asanoyama against Fujinokawa Saturday, ending about 5 a.m. ET. A win for Onosato plus losses for both leaves nobody able to reach 12 wins. Takanosho went kyujo (absent) on Day 13.

briefs.headline: Astros beat Athletics 7-5 to stay tied with the Rangers atop the AL West
briefs.summary: Lucas Spence hit the first three homers of his career Thursday night in West Sacramento. Texas closed its home schedule with a win over the Mets; both are 79-80 with three left, and Houston holds the tiebreaker from the season series.

briefs.headline: White Sox rout Royals 9-1 to clinch a playoff spot after two 100-loss seasons
briefs.summary: Chicago is the first team to follow consecutive 100-loss seasons with a postseason berth, AP reported; Thursday's win eliminated Baltimore. Cleveland also clinched with a shutout in Boston and leads the AL Central by one with three left.

briefs.headline: Padres beat Dodgers 4-2 to clinch a third straight postseason berth
briefs.summary: Fernando Tatis Jr. and Ethan Salas singled home runs in a three-run seventh Thursday night. The Cubs also clinched a wild card as Pete Crow-Armstrong reached 40 steals and 45 homers; Milwaukee, at 100 wins, kept Philadelphia from clinching.

briefs.headline: Falcons rout Packers 35-14 in Penix's return from ACL surgery
briefs.summary: Michael Penix Jr. went 18 of 25 for 256 yards and a touchdown Thursday night at Lambeau Field in his first game since November; Bijan Robinson ran for 194 yards and two scores. Green Bay is off to its worst start under Matt LaFleur.

briefs.headline: Lynx beat Fever 86-66 as the WNBA playoff seeds are set
briefs.summary: Kayla McBride scored 22 Thursday night and Caitlin Clark had two points on 1 of 12 shooting; Indiana drops to the No. 6 seed and opens at No. 3 Las Vegas. Top-seeded Minnesota faces New York. The playoffs open Sunday with four games.

briefs.headline: Sun beat Tempo 95-81 in the franchise's last game in Connecticut
briefs.summary: A sellout crowd of 8,911 at Mohegan Sun Arena saw the finale Thursday night before the team moves to Houston; Aaliyah Edwards had 14 first-half points. The Sun, in Connecticut since the 2002 season, finished with 11 wins and 33 losses.

coming_in.item: One day out. The archery and crossbow seasons for deer and for bear open tomorrow, Saturday, Sept. 26, and run through Dec. 31, with electronic registration required for both. The summary table carries no bag limit for either: deer limits are on pamphlet pages 13-18 and bear limits on pages 33-39, they vary by county and by permit class, and none is printed here.

coming_in.item: One day out. Wild boar archery and crossbow opens the same Saturday, Sept. 26, and runs through Dec. 31, with a second window Feb. 5-7; the season limit on the table is one, registration required. The gun season for boar is Oct. 24-31 with the same Feb. 5-7 second window.
coming_in.publication: West Virginia Hunting and Trapping Regulations Summary, July 2026 - June 2027

coming_in.item: Six days out. Crow season opens Thursday, Oct. 1, and runs through Nov. 21, with a second segment Jan. 1-March 6. The table prints no bag limit on the line and notes that nuisance crows committing depredations may be taken at any time.
coming_in.publication: West Virginia Hunting and Trapping Regulations Summary, July 2026 - June 2027

coming_in.item: Eight days out. The migratory bird summary, downloaded from wvdnr.gov and read again this morning, opens the regular duck season Saturday, Oct. 3, for a first segment through Oct. 11, then Nov. 7-15 and Dec. 21-Jan. 31. The daily bag is six ducks and the possession limit 18, in aggregate, with no more than four mallards (two of them hens), two black ducks, three pintails, three wood ducks, two redheads, two canvasbacks and four sea ducks; scaup carry their own line inside the six, one a day through Jan. 11 and two a day Jan. 12-31. Coots run the same dates at 15 and 45, mergansers at five and 15, and gallinules Oct. 3-11 and Dec. 2-Jan. 31 at 15 and 45. The second youth waterfowl day is Oct. 31. HIP registration and nontoxic shot are required, and a federal duck stamp for hunters 16 and older. Waterfowl hours at McClintic and Green Bottom WMAs end at noon Oct. 3-11, and McClintic's controlled area is permit-only those days.
coming_in.publication: West Virginia Migratory Bird Hunting Regulations Summary, September 2026 - January 2027

coming_in.item: Eight days out. The regular Canada and white-fronted goose season opens Saturday, Oct. 3, through Oct. 18, then Nov. 7-15 and Dec. 8-Jan. 31, five a day and 15 in possession in aggregate; snow and blue geese carry identical dates and limits, and brant is Jan. 2-31 at one and three. The early Canada goose season closed Sept. 13.
coming_in.publication: West Virginia Migratory Bird Hunting Regulations Summary, September 2026 - January 2027

coming_in.item: Eight days out. The third gun window for bear runs Oct. 3-9 in SELECTED COUNTIES. The summary table does not carry the county list, so no county is named here; the counties, rules and limits are on pamphlet pages 33-39 and vary by permit class. The table's own line reads one a day, two in possession and two a season, electronic registration required. Later windows are Oct. 22-25, Nov. 23-Dec. 6 and Dec. 7-31, all selected counties.
coming_in.publication: West Virginia Hunting and Trapping Regulations Summary, July 2026 - June 2027

prime.item: Day 14. Squirrel season opened Sept. 12 and runs through Feb. 28, six a day and 24 in possession, no season limit and no registration on the table.
prime.publication: West Virginia Hunting and Trapping Regulations Summary, July 2026 - June 2027

prime.item: Day 25, with 16 days left in the first segment, which closes Oct. 11; the second runs Nov. 2-15 and the third Dec. 7-Jan. 10, 15 a day and 45 in possession, hours a half hour before sunrise to sunset, HIP registration required. On the same table, read this morning: sora and Virginia rails through Nov. 9 at 10 and 30 in aggregate, Wilson's snipe through Dec. 16 at eight and 24, and woodcock opening Oct. 17 through Nov. 21 at three and nine, with a second segment Nov. 30-Dec. 8.
prime.publication: West Virginia Migratory Bird Hunting Regulations Summary, September 2026 - January 2027

prime.item: The Marine Fisheries recreational limits page, opened this morning and dated effective Sept. 2, 2026, prints red drum at 18 inches minimum and 27 inches maximum total length, one a day; its footnote C makes any red drum over 27 inches unlawful to possess and bars gigging, spearing or gaffing them. On today's Hampstead tides the drum window is the last of the ebb, the two hours before the 2:09 p.m. low, and again on the flood into the 8:08 p.m. high, the day before the full moon. The Fisherman's Post September report, published Sept. 1 and 24 days old with nothing newer on its feed this morning, is the month's pattern, not the day's: Native Son had a steady bite at docks and creek mouths on topwater early and natural bait as the sun climbed, Spring Tide had over-slot schools of 28 to 32 inches that do not hold in one place, fish over the maximum that go back, and Speckled Specialist had reds in small groups on oysters, docks, grass points and ledges. Coastal Angler's Topsail column, also Sept. 1 and 24 days old, called September its favorite drum month, the shrimp bigger and moving, and threw gold spoons, topwater and soft plastics at slot fish.

Limits page: 14 to 20 inches total length, three a day, with one of the three allowed over 26 inches. Dusk and the dock lights on the ebb after the 8:08 p.m. high are the window on today's tide, with the water at Beaufort down to 72.7 degrees this morning. The Sept. 1 shop reports, 24 days old, had trout numbers uneven trip to trip with the size good, the occasional fish from Native Son, and the Jolly Roger and Surf City piers taking them in the bottom fishing early and in the evening; Coastal Angler's Sept. 1 column fished them on drop-offs and pot holes with a MirrOlure, a curly tail under a popping cork and a 17MR.

prime.species: Spanish mackerel, bluefish and king mackerel
prime.item: Limits page: Spanish mackerel 12-inch fork length, 15 a day; king mackerel 24-inch fork length, three a day, both carrying footnote H, which points to the South Atlantic council and the most recent mackerel proclamation for seasons; bluefish no minimum, and footnote M, read again this morning, sets the creel by proclamation at five per person per day in all private, non-for-hire fisheries and up to seven per person on a for-hire vessel, so the table's 5/Day line is the private figure. Today is not the day for them: the Wilmington surf zone forecast, issued 3:06 a.m., has surf 3 to 5 feet on a north wind around 15 mph and a high rip current risk through this evening, against the calm early-and-late surface bite on Gotcha plugs and casting jigs the Sept. 1 pier reports described. Those reports, 24 days old, had East Coast Sports still waiting on the fall king bite at the pier ends and South End Adventures finding kings 8 to 12 miles out.

Limits page: black drum 14 inches minimum and 25 inches maximum total length, 10 a day, with footnote C allowing one over 25 inches; sheepshead 14 inches total length, five a day. Both fish want moving water against structure, so the pilings and oyster rocks on the ebb toward 2:09 p.m. or the flood after it, not the slack. Surf City Pier reported black drum, pompano and croakers in the bottom fishing on Sept. 1, Jolly Roger Pier had black drum with red drum and Virginia mullet, and Coastal Angler's Sept. 1 column had black drum on cut shrimp at bridges, docks and deep oyster rocks; all three are 24 days old.

going_out.item: Closes today. The second gun window for bear, open since Saturday, Sept. 19, ends today, Friday, Sept. 25, in SELECTED COUNTIES; the summary table does not carry the county list, so no county is named here, and the county rules and limits are on pamphlet pages 33-39 and vary by permit class. Electronic registration is required. The next gun window is Oct. 3-9, eight days out.
going_out.publication: West Virginia Hunting and Trapping Regulations Summary, July 2026 - June 2027

going_out.item: Five days left in the closure after today. The Marine Fisheries limits page, effective Sept. 2, 2026, prints flounder of all species 'Sep 1-14: OPEN, Sep 15-30: CLOSED, UNLAWFUL TO POSSESS,' so the fish is release-only through Wednesday, Sept. 30. The Sept. 1 shop reports that had flounder 'all over the place' and a 20-to-24-inch class at Carolina Flats were written with harvest open and are 24 days old.

sections.note: Every West Virginia hunting date above was read from reference/wv-hunting-2026-27.json, which is valid through June 30, 2027, and was checked against today's date, Sept. 25, 2026; the county lists for the selected-counties bear windows and the deer and bear limits are not in that table and are not printed. The migratory bird PDF was downloaded from wvdnr.gov with plain curl this morning, with certificate verification on, opened with PyMuPDF, and its seasons table was rendered to an image to read the scaup line, so every migratory date and limit above is this morning's read. The North Carolina limits are copied from the Division of Marine Fisheries recreational size and bag limits page, which is dated effective Sept. 2, 2026, and which still prints flounder 'Sep 15-30: CLOSED, unlawful to possess' for all species; the closure has five days left after today. The page's footnote M now reads five bluefish per person per day in private fisheries and seven on a for-hire vessel. The Gauley release schedule is still reported, not confirmed: the Corps' Huntington District Summersville page failed certificate verification with plain curl this morning and was not retried with verification off, and its water-management site answered 503. On the USGS gauges, the Gauley above Belva, 03192000, read 5,260 cfs at 5 a.m. after rising overnight from 4,410 at 5 a.m. Thursday to 5,380 at 1 a.m., and the stage-only gauge below Summersville Dam, 03189600, stepped from 11.90 feet at 2 p.m. Thursday to 12.27 at 4 p.m. and held 12.26 to 12.29 through 4:45 a.m.; whether the dam is releasing cannot be told from those numbers by this desk. A search for WVDNR trout stocking in September turned up only the spring stocking stories and the agency's stocking page, so no stocking line runs.

sections.label: On the Water

waters.reading: 950.0 cfs, 3.71 feet at 5:15 a.m., flagged falling against 1410.0 cfs and 4.34 feet in the fetcher's comparison.
waters.read: 950 cfs - blown out. Stay on the bank.
waters.working: Coming off a second crest, still too high, and falling since 1:15 p.m. Thursday. The USGS two-day trace, pulled at 5:52 a.m., has the river finishing Wednesday's recession at a low of 721 cfs and 3.34 feet at 2:15 a.m. Thursday, then rising again through Thursday morning: 767 at 6 a.m., 903 at 8, 1,470 at 10, 1,630 at noon and a crest of 1,660 cfs and 4.64 feet at 1:15 p.m. Thursday, a foot above the overnight low. From there it has shed water without a pause: 1,560 at 4 p.m., 1,460 at 6, 1,340 at 8, 1,240 at 10, 1,130 at midnight, 1,050 at 2 a.m., 983 at 4 and 950 at 5 and 5:15, about 45 cfs an hour on Thursday afternoon and 33 an hour overnight. Against the true 24-hour mark, 755 cfs and 3.40 feet at 5:15 a.m. Thursday, the river is up 195 cfs and 0.31 feet on the day. The fetcher's 1,410 cfs and 4.34 feet are the first point of its two-day window, 6 a.m. Wednesday, on the tail of Tuesday night's crest, not 24 hours ago, which is why its flag reads falling on a river that is higher than it was at this hour Thursday; the flag is wrong on the day and right on the last 16 hours. What lifted the river Thursday morning, the gauge does not say; the Weather Service's products on the headwaters this morning are a Frost Advisory for Northwest Pocahontas until 9 a.m., with temperatures as low as 33, and Charleston's 3:56 a.m. statement on valley fog covering Northwest Webster and Northwest Nicholas. The read string is the fetcher's flow-band verdict and stands: at 950 cfs the pocket water is still one channel, the plunge pools are still pushing stained, and the undercut banks are still under the river. At the overnight rate the 500-cfs line is about 14 hours below this morning's reading and the 300-cfs line a day and a half, if the recession holds. When it drops into the seams, the forage after three flushes in a week is what the bottom gave up, stonefly nymphs and sculpin, fished on the inside edges of the plunge-pool tailouts and along the undercut banks where the current first eases; the caddis and the long leader come back with the clarity, and that is a different river from this one.
waters.note: The fetcher's 1410.0 cfs and 4.34 feet comparison point is the first point of its two-day window, 6 a.m. Wednesday, not 24 hours ago; the trace's true 24-hour mark is 755 cfs and 3.40 feet at 5:15 a.m. Thursday, so the falling flag is wrong on the day, up 195 cfs, and right only on the 16 hours since the second crest, 1,660 cfs and 4.64 feet at 1:15 p.m. Thursday. The fetcher's numbers, flag and read string are printed as written; the Thursday low, the second crest and the overnight recession are the trace's. No water temperature came back from the gauge. The Weather Service's active list for West Virginia at 5:52 a.m. carries four products: Charleston's Special Weather Statement on valley fog, which names Northwest Webster and Northwest Nicholas among 26 zones, and Frost Advisories until 8 or 9 a.m. on Pocahontas, Randolph, Grant, Pendleton, Preston and Tucker.

waters.near: 14 miles above R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.reading: 26.61 feet at 5 a.m., flagged rising against 25.93 in the fetcher's comparison.
waters.read: 26.6 ft and rising — normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: At normal pool, up two-thirds of a foot on the day and flat since 3 a.m. The trace has the pool bottoming at 25.35 feet at 5:45 p.m. Wednesday and rising through Thursday: 25.98 at 5 a.m. Thursday, the true 24-hour mark, 26.03 at 6 a.m., 26.17 at 8, 26.33 at 1 p.m., 26.35 at 3, a dip to 26.24 at 7 and 9 p.m., then 26.31 at 11 p.m., 26.46 at 1 a.m., 26.62 at 3 a.m. and a window high of 26.63 at 2:45 and 3:30 a.m., with the last three hours holding between 26.60 and 26.63. Against the 24-hour mark the gauge is up 0.63 feet, so the fetcher's rising flag is right on the day; its 25.93 is the first point of its two-day window, 6 a.m. Wednesday, not 24 hours ago, and by luck it sits within a twentieth of a foot of the true mark. The gauge does not say what is coming down. The Kanawha enters the Ohio at Point Pleasant, and the Gauley, which joins the New to form it, rose overnight on its own USGS gauge above Belva from 4,410 cfs at 5 a.m. Thursday to 5,380 at 1 a.m. and 5,260 at 5 a.m. with no rain product anywhere in the state. The read string is the fetcher's stage-band verdict for 26.6 and 'rising' is the fetcher's word; the pool is normal and the bank access ordinary. A pool at 26.6 with a push of Kanawha water arriving behind it fishes the structure that has current on it: the upstream faces and tips of the wing dams and the riprap points, where the shad and skipjack get pinned against the rock as the flow picks up. A white or pearl swimbait on a half-ounce head swum along the wing-dam faces is the shad pattern for hybrids and white bass while the water carries color, a black-and-blue jig with a crawfish trailer worked down the riprap is the pattern on the rock, and the barge-cut mouths and the creek mouths on the Mason side will hold the color longest. Mason County is under no Weather Service product this morning.
waters.note: This is the pool side, 14 miles above R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam; USGS does not gauge the Byrd tailwater. The fetcher's 25.93 is the first point of its two-day window, 6 a.m. Wednesday, not 24 hours ago, and its rising flag compares 26.61 against that; the trace's true 24-hour change is up 0.63 feet from 25.98 at 5 a.m. Thursday, the low was 25.35 at 5:45 p.m. Wednesday, the window high 26.63 at 2:45 and 3:30 a.m. today, and the direction in the last three hours is flat. The fetcher's numbers and read string are printed as written; the low, the Thursday rise and the overnight high are the trace's. The Weather Service's NWPS page for Point Pleasant, PTPW2, is on the blocked list and was not retried, so no forecast is printed for this gauge; the Gauley figures are from USGS 03192000, pulled at 5:52 a.m.

waters.near: below R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.reading: 30.19 feet at 5 a.m., flagged falling against 31.83 in the fetcher's comparison.
waters.read: 30.2 ft and falling — up and pushing. Expect colour and current; fish the slack behind anything solid.
waters.working: Up a foot and a half on the day and forecast to crest tonight. The trace has the river bottoming at 28.73 feet at 5 a.m. Thursday, the true 24-hour mark and the lowest point in the two-day window, and rising ever since: 28.77 at 6 a.m., 28.84 at 8, 29.11 at 11, 29.29 at 3 p.m., 29.58 at 7 p.m., 29.88 at 11 p.m., 30.09 at 1 a.m., 30.01 at 3, 30.26 at 4:45 and 30.19 at 5 a.m., the last three hours bouncing between 30.01 and 30.26 with the trend up. That is up 1.46 feet on the day and up at 5 a.m., so the fetcher's falling flag is wrong on both counts: its 31.83 is the first point of its two-day window, 6 a.m. Wednesday, on the recession from Tuesday's crest, and the river is now below that point only because it fell 3.1 feet Wednesday before turning. The Weather Service's NWPS gauge for Huntington read 30.27 at 5 a.m., eight-hundredths over USGS, and its forecast, issued 10:44 a.m. Thursday, has the rise continuing: 31.1 at 8 a.m. today, 31.6 at 2 p.m., a crest of 31.8 at 8 p.m. tonight, 31.6 at 2 a.m. Saturday, 31.1 at 8 a.m., 30.5 at 2 p.m. and 29.6 by 8 p.m. Saturday, 28.6 at 2 a.m. Sunday, 27.8 at 8 a.m., 27.2 by Sunday night, 26.9 Monday morning and 26.2 by 8 a.m. Tuesday, with no flooding category at any point; its 30.2 for 2 a.m. today matched the gauge within a tenth. Action stage is 48 feet and minor flood 50. The read string is the fetcher's stage-band verdict for 30.2, and 'up and pushing' is the fetcher's phrase for the band; here the direction is the fetcher's error and the band is right. A rising, coloring river below a dam puts the fish in the slack rather than on the seams: the eddy behind the lock wall, the downstream pockets of the wing dams and the first riprap below the barge cuts, where the shad and skipjack pile up out of the push. Live shad or cut skipjack on a bottom rig in that slack is the catfish pattern on a rise, a three-inch white swimbait or a skipjack-pattern jerkbait worked along the eddy line is the pattern for hybrids and white bass, and the crawfish jig on the riprap waits for the drop the forecast puts at Saturday afternoon. Cabell County is under Charleston's 3:56 a.m. statement on dense valley fog and no other product this morning.
waters.note: This is the gauge below R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam, not the tailwater. The fetcher's 31.83 is the first point of its two-day window, 6 a.m. Wednesday, not 24 hours ago; the trace's true 24-hour change is up 1.46 feet from 28.73 at 5 a.m. Thursday, which is also the window's low, and the direction at 5 a.m. is up, so the fetcher's falling flag is wrong on both counts. The fetcher's numbers and read string are printed as written; the low and the Thursday rise are the trace's. The NWPS forecast quoted is the one issued 14:44 UTC Thursday, 10:44 a.m. ET, read from the stageflow endpoint at 5:52 a.m., and it replaces Wednesday night's forecast, which had a 29.7-foot crest this morning; the new crest is 31.8 at 8 p.m. tonight. The flood categories are from the HNTW2 gauge page. The Corps' Huntington District site failed certificate verification and no lock notice is printed.

waters.reading: Sound at Hampstead: low 1:48 AM at 0.7 ft, high 7:46 AM at 3.9 ft, low 2:09 PM at 0.7 ft, high 8:08 PM at 4.1 ft. Surf at Ocean City Beach pier: low 12:48 AM at 0.5 ft, high 6:57 AM at 4.8 ft, low 1:01 PM at 0.3 ft, high 7:17 PM at 5.0 ft. Water 72.7F at Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast. Moon waxing gibbous, 98% lit, 13.6 days old.
waters.read: Fish the moving water either side of high at 7:46 AM and 8:08 PM in the sound.
waters.working: The day before the full moon, and the springs are at the top of the cycle: the U.S. Naval Observatory's phase table, read this morning, puts the full moon at Sept. 26, 16:49 Universal Time, 12:49 p.m. ET Saturday, and the last quarter at Oct. 3, so at 13.6 days the moon is a day from full, the swings are the biggest of the month and the inlet current is running hard. The sound at Hampstead drains 3.2 feet from the 7:46 a.m. high to the 2:09 p.m. low and fills 3.4 feet to the 8:08 p.m. high, the day's biggest move; the surf high at 7:17 p.m. is 5.0 feet. Today the sound runs 49 minutes behind the inlet on the morning high, 68 on the midday low and 51 on the evening high, the low lagging most, which stretches the ebb at the crew's water. Red drum want the last of the fall, and at Hampstead that is the two hours before 2:09 p.m., when the draining marsh pushes shrimp and finger mullet out of the grass into the creek channels and the drum wait on the oyster bars and creek mouths below: a live finger mullet or cut mullet on a Carolina rig a couple of feet off the channel edge, or the gold spoon and topwater the Sept. 1 reports threw in the mornings. The flood from 2:09 to the 8:08 p.m. high puts drum onto the flooded grass edges and the dock flats in the last hour of light, the secondary window, and the fetcher's read has the moving water either side of 8:08 as the evening. The ebb after dark under a near-full moon is the dock-light pattern: a small paddletail or a shrimp imitation on a light jighead drifted through the edge of the light for trout and the shrimp they are on. Sheepshead take a fiddler crab tight to the pilings on either moving tide, and nothing wants the slack at 2:09 or 8:08. The water at Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast, is 72.7, down 4.1 degrees from Thursday's reading at the same station after two nights of north wind. The Fisherman's Post September report, published Sept. 1 and 24 days old with nothing newer on the feed this morning, is the month's pattern, not the day's water: Native Son on a steady drum bite at docks and creek mouths, topwater early and natural bait as the sun climbed; Spring Tide on over-slot schools of 28 to 32 inches that do not stay put; Speckled Specialist on reds in small groups on oysters, docks, grass points and ledges; Carolina Flats on mullet thick inshore; both piers taking black drum and Virginia mullet on the bottom. Coastal Angler's Topsail column, also Sept. 1 and 24 days old, had black drum on cut shrimp at bridges, docks and deep oyster rocks and slot reds on gold spoons, topwater and soft plastics. Flounder remain closed and unlawful to possess through Sept. 30 on the Marine Fisheries limits page opened this morning. Beach: NWS Wilmington's Rip Current Statement for Coastal Pender, issued 1:32 a.m., carries a high rip current risk through 8 p.m. tonight and a Coastal Flood Advisory from 5 to 9 a.m. for up to a foot of inundation in low-lying spots along the Intracoastal Waterway and the tidal creeks, on the morning high; its surf zone forecast for Surf City and Topsail Beach, issued 3:06 a.m., has surf 3 to 5 feet on a north wind around 15 mph, partly sunny with highs in the lower 70s and the water in the upper 70s, the risk high again Saturday at 3 to 4 feet on a northwest wind around 10, then low Sunday at 2 to 3 feet, low Monday at around a foot on a northwest wind around 5, and low Tuesday at around a foot on an east wind around 5. That is not the calm-morning, bait-tight-to-the-beach setup the pier reports described for Spanish and bluefish on Gotcha plugs, and the surf does not lie down until Sunday.

Coastal Angler's Topsail column is also Sept. 1, 24 days old, and its author feed has nothing newer for Topsail. Both are the month's pattern, not this morning's water, and both were written while flounder harvest was open. The fetcher's sound and surf tables today carry all four events inside Friday and no event carries a weekday spillover tag. The Rip Current Statement and Coastal Flood Advisory on Coastal Pender are Wilmington's products for the Topsail coast at 5:52 a.m.; Coastal New Hanover has the same pair, Coastal Brunswick and Inland New Hanover have Coastal Flood Advisories, Coastal Onslow has a Beach Hazards Statement from the Newport office from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m., and the rest of the state's 22 active products are Coastal Flood Warnings and Advisories, High Surf Advisories, Beach Hazards Statements and a Wind Advisory from Carteret north to Currituck. The National Hurricane Center's 2 a.m. outlook has newly formed Tropical Storm Gonzalo about 160 miles east-southeast of the southernmost Cabo Verde Islands and Tropical Storm Fay well to the west-southwest of the Azores, with no tropical cyclone formation expected in the next seven days; nothing is forecast toward the Carolinas. The full-moon and last-quarter dates are from the USNO phases API, read this morning. Hampstead is the sound station and the tide that matters; the water temperature is Beaufort's, 60 miles up the coast, not the sound's, and Thursday's 76.8 is from Thursday's edition.
